sections.title: What this office does
sections.text:
What this office does

Your senator votes on national laws, the federal budget, and treaties, and votes yes or no on judges and cabinet officials the President picks. They can't fix a pothole or change a state law. Call them about federal issues — Social Security, veterans' benefits, immigration cases, or how they should vote on a bill.

U.S. Constitution, Article I

What this bill does — plain language

Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money.
